evidence.curator_note: Eq 8.1, left-column double-arrow equilibrium labeled 'rH' with delta(dHf) = -0.6 eV connecting the top structure (pent-2-ene molecular ion, dHf/IE 8.7(9.0)) and the middle structure (pent-1-ene molecular ion, drawn folded with the transferring H flagged, (30%), dHf/IE 9.3(9.5)). This is an isomerization (double-bond migration), not a fragmentation: a 1,3-hydrogen shift interconverts the two C5H10 radical cations. Book draws 0 curved arcs on this page (it is an energetics/reaction scheme, not an arrow-pushing figure). A faithful 1,3-H ATOM transfer needs 3 fishhooks (odd electron -> forming C-H, gamma C-H -> forming C-H, that C-H -> the vacated carbon); the migrating H cannot be atom-mapped because RDKit folds any mapped explicit H into implicit valence, so only the surviving heavy-atom change is encoded: the odd electron relocating from C1 to C3 (a single fishhook atom(1)->atom(3)). The H migrates the opposite way (C3->C1) and is written implicitly in the product SMILES (C1: .CH2 -> CH3; C3: CH2 -> .CH). LOCALIZATION (convention C): both C5H10(+.) ions are drawn by McLafferty as intact alkenes with a delocalized (+.); encoded here as the opened (distonic) localized resonance form (cation on C2, odd electron on the terminal that carries it) so the arrow has a real origin. Direction shown 1-pentene -> 2-pentene to match the MOD rule; the page draws it as an equilibrium (reversible).

Cross-linked MOD rule IMS_8_1_var1_step1 ('monomolecular ion-cleavage 8.1 rH -0.6'), verified against this scheme. Its DFS '[H]1[C]2..[C]5..[C]8([H]9)([H]10)[C]11([H]12){=}[C+.]13([H]14)([H]15) >> ..[C]8([H]9){=}[C]11([H]12)[C+.]13([H]14)([H]15)([H]10)' is exactly a 1,3-H shift: H10 moves from the gamma carbon C8 to the terminal C13, the C11=C13 double bond becomes C8=C11, and the charge/odd-electron site shifts accordingly (their C13/C11/C8 = the terminal / internal-alkene / gamma carbons; my C1/C2/C3). CONNECTIVITY MATCHES. REPRESENTATION DIFFERENCE (not a defect of this scheme): the MOD rule keeps the double bond and writes the whole (+.) on one terminal carbon as [C+.] bearing a double bond plus two H -- formally over-valent and not RDKit-parseable -- a German-edition localization device; this record uses the RDKit-valid opened distonic form instead.
